claims.text: The initial system is a pristine, equimolar, FCC FeNiCrCoCu single-crystal coating on a single-crystal Cu matrix at 300 K.
The proposed simulations use nanoindentation to 30 Å at 10 m/s and temperatures of 300, 600, 900, and 1200 K.
Above 900 K, a cascade involving stacking faults, phase transformation, amorphization, and dislocation starvation causes the friction spike and collapse of wear resistance.
Thermally activated partial-dislocation nucleation leads to rapid stacking-fault accumulation.
Thermal unlocking of Lomer-Cottrell locks accelerates stacking-fault annihilation and triggers or promotes an FCC-to-HCP martensitic transformation.
Coalescing HCP regions form brittle pathways that facilitate the onset of shear-induced amorphization.
HCP regions have insufficient active slip systems, causing dislocation starvation and catastrophic loss of load-bearing capacity.
Phase-transformation-driven mechanical annealing eliminates ductile FCC slip pathways and thereby increases friction and reduces wear resistance.
The friction coefficient increases by more than 40% above 900 K.
Hardness decreases by more than 50% at 1200 K.
Wear volume increases exponentially with temperature.
The HCP phase fraction exceeds 30% at 1200 K.
Amorphous zones appear in the nanoindentation tracks at high temperature.
Between 300 and 600 K, dislocation density decreases slightly and elastic modulus consequently increases.
Between 300 and 600 K, the FCC structure remains stable without significant HCP formation or amorphization.
The hypothesis is restricted to single-crystal FeNiCrCoCu coatings on Cu matrices under nanoindentation and is not asserted for polycrystals or other substrates.
Local chemical short-range order may shift the temperature at which amorphization begins.
Thermal vibrations above 1000 K may confound dislocation-line-length measurements.
HCP atom count, dislocation line length, and amorphous-zone fraction can be tracked using CNA, DXA, and bond-angle distributions, respectively.

The hypothesis is falsified if the 1200 K HCP fraction remains below 10% despite a friction spike, dislocation line length rises monotonically without unlocking events, or amorphous zones fail to correlate with wear-resistance loss; a 600 K simulation serves as the control.
